articles.title: Soldado da PM morre após acidente com motocicleta na Bahia  | G1
articles.standfirst: Situação aconteceu no município de Cansanção, no norte do estado. Oderlan Santiago Alves, estava a trabalho no momento em que morreu.
articles.summary: Situação aconteceu no município de Cansanção, no norte do estado. Oderlan Santiago Alves, estava a trabalho no momento em que morreu.
articles.body:
Soldado da PM morre após acidente com motocicleta na Bahia — Foto: Redes Sociais

Um soldado da Polícia Militar (PM) morreu após uma batida envolvendo a motocicleta que pilotava, nesta sexta-feira (30), na cidade de Cansanção , no norte da Bahia.

Informações apuradas pela TV Bahia apontam que a vítima tentava fazer uma ultrapassagem quando bateu em uma retroescavadeira. A situação aconteceu na localidade de Lagoa dos Cavalos, na zona rural do município.

Segundo a PM, o militar, identificado como Oderlan Santiago Alves , estava a trabalho no momento em que morreu. Ele integrava uma equipe da 7ª CIPM que se deslocava para Monte Santo , onde participaria do policiamento da Operação Festa de Todos os Santos.

A vítima morreu no local do acidente, logo após a batida. O corpo foi encaminhado para o Instituto Médico Legal (IML), para necropsia. Não há detalhes sobre o sepultamento. O caso foi registrado na Delegacia de Cansanção.

Em nota, a PM manifestou profundo pesar pela morte do soldado e se solidarizou com familiares, amigos e colegas de farda neste momento de dor.

articles.title: Algunos comercios de Madrid y Valencia se blindan ante posibles saqueos durante la noche de Halloween
articles.standfirst: Han tapiado sus escaparates o adelantarán sus horarios de cierre
articles.summary: Han tapiado sus escaparates o adelantarán sus horarios de cierre
articles.body: Las tiendas de algunas de las calles principales de las ciudades de Madrid y Valencia están blindándose y protegiéndose ante la posibilidad de que se produzcan disturbios y saqueos a lo largo de este fin de semana. Varios comercios han tapiado sus escaparates con paneles de madera y otros estudian adelantar sus horarios de cierre o no abrir sus puertas este sábado, 31 de octubre, noche de Halloween. El motivo se debe a los llamamientos que difundió la organización Blocus en redes sociales y diferentes canales de mensajería, animando a protagonizar actos vandálicos y saqueos, coincidiendo con esta celebración. Todo llega tras los altercados que tuvieron lugar recientemente en Barcelona y Bilbao. En la capital de España, algunas tiendas de la calle Fuencarral, Preciados y alrededores de Sol y Gran Vía han comenzado a proteger sus escaparates. Decathlon, Orange o Foot Locker han tomado medidas al respecto. En Valencia, la situación también preocupa. En la calle Colón, tiendas como Zara y Lefties están colocando paneles de madera para proteger sus cristales. Otros negocios y cafeterías del lugar adelantarán sus cierres, algunos a partir de las 16:30 horas. La presencia policial en ambas ciudades se duplicará por la noche de Halloween y ante esta posibilidad de saqueos. Asimismo, instan a los ciudadanos a evitar acudir al centro de las urbes durante la tarde-noche de este sábado, 31 de octubre. Cabe destacar que ante la convocatoria de la organización Blocus, la Policía Nacional detuvo a varios jóvenes que estarían supuestamente relacionados con los llamamientos a los saqueos. Entre ellos, figura un menor de 17 años que estaría detrás de los canales de comunicación, y otro de 18 años al que se le atribuye la incitación a fabricar y a arrojar cócteles molotov.

articles.title: Police deployed during stand-off over control of top Poland court
articles.summary: The escalation came after the government suspended two senior justices and moved to bring criminal charges against them.
articles.body:
Riot police have been deployed at Poland's Constitutional Court amid an escalating stand-off between the government and the court's top judges.

The row pits the government of Prime Minister Donald Tusk against his predecessors from the right-wing Law and Justice (PiS).

The police intervention came after Justice Minister Waldemar Żurek said he had requested stripping the court's President Bogdan Święczkowski and Vice-President Bartłomiej Sochański of their immunity from prosecution to bring criminal charges against them.

Tusk has vowed to depoliticise the judiciary, and on Friday defended the move as PiS supporters gathered outside the court premises in Warsaw in protest.

Riot police were deployed to prevent any demonstrators from entering the court building.

In a social media post, the Constitutional Court wrote that the two judges the government wants to prosecute were still the legally appointed senior justices of the court.

"All persons participating in these actions are committing the crime of a coup d'etat," it said.

In a social media post, Tusk wrote: "Restoring the rule of law is our duty. After years of Law and Justice's lawlessness, this is a difficult, sometimes painful process that requires decisive action. There is no other way."

President Karol Nawrocki, who is backed by PiS, ordered his plane be turned back to Warsaw on his way to Senegal to attend the Summer Youth Olympic Games.

The PiS-led government took office in 2015 and moved swiftly to appoint judges to the court to gain a majority there because the court has the power to decide on the legality of legislation.

Leading European courts - the European Court of Human Rights and the Court of Justice of the European Union - subsequently ruled the PiS majority had elected three of the judges improperly because they were duplicating positions that had been validly filled by the previous parliament.

The European courts ruled Poland's Constitutional Court was no longer an "independent and impartial tribunal", and Tusk's government has used those rulings as a basis to stop publishing the tribunal's rulings.

Tusk has failed to undo the PiS-era changes, partially because Nawrocki and his PiS-backed predecessor Andrzej Duda used their presidential vetoes to block his attempts.

Nawrocki has also refused to swear in five Constitutional Court judges elected by parliament since March on the grounds of alleged flaws in their selection procedure.

One of those judges, Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, has now been placed in temporary charge of the court.

Earlier this month, the Council of Europe's advisory body on constitutional matters, the Venice Commission, said Nawrocki should swear-in the judges to allow them to sit on the court's bench.

Justice Minister Żurek said Święczkowski and his vice-president should face criminal charges for not allowing the judges to adjudicate.

Some of Tusk's supporters have accused him of failing to act decisively to reverse the PiS-era reforms.

Parliamentary elections are scheduled next year, and some see his move as an attempt to boost Tusk's popularity among those voters.

But his actions have been criticised. In September, Tusk put forward a politician, Maciej Berek, a lawyer who served as a minister in his cabinet, as a judge candidate to the court.

Lawyer Marcin Matczak, a critic of the PiS-era judicial reform who has stated he considers Święczkowski to be the court's worst president, said his suspension had no legal basis "for a million reasons".

"Today's action at the Constitutional Court, in my opinion, buries this body and the issue of the rule of law for two decades," Prof Matczak wrote on social media.

"Images of armed police and legal interpretations according to which the minister of justice can remove the president of the Constitutional Court by decree will have a powerful, anti-rule of law backlash for years to come," he added.

articles.title: California dad of 5 says charter school rejected books that even mentioned God: 'Publisher blacklist'
articles.summary: John Woolard says a California charter school rejected homeschooling materials that merely mentioned God, forcing his family to pay out of pocket.
articles.body: A California father of five says his family's public charter school rejected homeschooling materials that merely mentioned God or faith, even when the books met state academic standards, forcing his family to pay out of pocket for educational resources he says other parents could access with public funds. John Woolard told Fox News Digital he and his wife initially had no problems using a public charter school program that allowed them to educate their children at home. But he said they eventually discovered that their curriculum choices were being scrutinized for religious content. "Any book or curriculum purchase that we wanted to make that referenced God or faith in even, like, an adjacent sort of way was being denied," Woolard said. CALIFORNIA SCHOOL DISTRICT SUED OVER FIELD TRIP TO MOSQUE WHERE STUDENTS ALLEGEDLY DONNED MUSLIM GARB He described what he called a "publisher blacklist" and said the restrictions extended beyond explicitly Christian instructional materials. Woolard said he even encountered problems with books examining the religious beliefs of America's Founding Fathers. "You would think that that would be something that would be non-controversial, but those curriculum choices would be denied," he said. For Woolard, the dispute goes beyond religious expression. As a father of five, he said, the charter school program provided a cost-effective way to tailor the curriculum to each child's individual needs. But when the school rejected certain curriculum purchases, he said, his family was left covering the costs. "If our curriculum choices are denied, then we have to pay for those resources. We have to pay for those curriculum choices out of pocket," Woolard told Fox News Digital. WASHINGTON FATHER SUES SCHOOL DISTRICT FOR DENYING RELIGIOUS OPT-OUT FOR FIFTH GRADER FROM LGBTQ INSTRUCTION Woolard said he pressed school officials to explain why the materials were being rejected. He asked whether the curriculum met California standards and whether it was academically rigorous enough. According to Woolard, the answer to both questions was yes. "So, at the end of the day, the only objection that you have to this curriculum, our curriculum choices, is that there's a faith component to it," Woolard said he recalled asking. He said both a teacher and principal acknowledged that the religious component was the objection. WASHINGTON SCHOOL DISTRICT THAT FORCED KIDS TO HIDE BIBLES IN SEALED ENVELOPES MUST APOLOGIZE, PAY $275K "What that tells me is that equality only extends as far as what the government approves," he said. Stephanie Taub, senior counsel with First Liberty Institute, characterized the policy as discriminatory toward families seeking a faith-based education during an interview with Fox News Digital. "What we're asking here is California has a policy that singles out parents who want to give their children a faith-based education, and it excludes them from homeschooling benefits that would otherwise be available," the attorney said. Taub said the family is seeking s after an unfavorable lower-court decision. Woolard said he hopes the justices will ultimately force California to change its approach. "What I really hope is for the government or for the Supreme Court to come back and tell California you got the decision wrong, and this is the way to correct it," he said. He added that such a ruling could "break open California for a lot of families" seeking similar changes. Taub said the Supreme Court is considering whether to take the case and that she expects to hear whether the justices will review it in the next few months. articles.title: Polish police deployed to top court after head judge suspended
articles.summary: Judge’s suspension is part of a long dispute over politicisation of the Constitutional Tribunal under former government.
articles.body:
Polish police have been deployed outside the country’s top court after demonstrators gathered to protest the suspension of its head judge.

Police said on Friday they entered the premises of the Constitutional Tribunal after incidents outside the court, including objects being thrown at police.

Protesters descended on the Warsaw court after it announced on Friday that its head, Bogdan Swieczkowski, had been suspended.

His suspension is related to a long-running dispute that has effectively paralysed the court.

Over the past six months, Swieczkowski used his power as head of the court to block judges elected by the current parliamentary majority from assuming their court duties.

Minister of Justice Waldemar Zurek told reporters on Friday that he had requested that Swieczkowski and his deputy’s immunity be lifted for failing to fulfil their duties by preventing judges from performing their work.

Swieczkowski was appointed to his position by Poland’s former nationalist Law and Justice party (PiS) government, which critics have accused of politicising the country’s courts.

Restoring the rule of law ⁠is the government’s duty, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on X following the news of Swieczkowski’s suspension.

“After years ⁠of lawlessness under PiS, this process ⁠is difficult, at times even painful, and requires decisive action. There is no other way,” said Tusk, leader of the Civic Coalition party.

News of Swieczkowski’s suspension brought crowds of PiS supporters to the gates of the Constitutional Tribunal. Police said they detained three people after some in the crowd launched “dangerous projectiles”.

Also on Friday, PiS-allied Polish President Karol Nawrocki announced he was turning his plane around while on the way to a sporting event in Senegal, saying: “At a moment like this, the President must be in Poland”.

Since his election in mid-2025, Nawrocki has refused to swear in three ⁠of six judges nominated by the Polish parliament.

Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal has long been a point of serious political contention, with critics in Poland and across the European Union accusing PiS, which led the country from 2015 to 2023, of imposing political control over the court by electing judges friendly to the party and its policies.

When Poland’s pro-European government came to power, it promised to restore the independence of the judiciary. However, two attempts to do so have been vetoed by two PiS-aligned presidents – one of them Nawrocki.

Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, one of the judges Nawrocki refused to swear in on the grounds of alleged flaws in her selection procedure, has now been placed in charge of the Constitutional Tribunal.

Politicians from PiS, currently Poland’s largest opposition force, have criticised Swieczkowski’s suspension.

“This is a blatant, criminal attack on the constitutional order,” former Justice Minister Zbigniew Ziobro wrote on X Friday.
